chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Ben Pollack: drummer-bandleader who claimed credit for others
summary: Pollack, a former drummer with a Palm Springs club, boasted of discovering musicians; Horace wrote for him in Chicago early on.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Ben Pollock. There's a historical man.
Yes, there's a lot of history behind that guy, because he had quite a few names that he started out, and Ben would tell you, he's another little active guy too. He would

really talk. He was a drummer, you know, at one time. He used to play drums, and, you know, he'd have that two-week beat thing going, you know, but he had a lot of great names that at one time had started out with him, and he would let you know too -- "I was responsible for this guy."

-- you know, and I think the last I heard of Ben, that he was running a club of his own in Palm Springs, and he just recently passed, and it was too bad because he was a legend. He recorded with his band and whatnot. A lot of people knew him.
When did you write for him? Was that in the early days or --
I think that was the early days, yes, early days. And this was around Chicago. Because... It was --
That's mainly where he was operating.

Yes, right. And, of course, I was a free lancer then, and I made one or two things for him and tried, and it worked out all right, and he says to me, "Well, when you get some spare time, make some more," you know. The guys in those days, they were very encouraging to you, especially if they knew you were pursuing that field; they wanted to help you out. At the same time you were helping them.
So it worked out for both parties
